articles.title: Un tridente... y un sonrojante 19-5
articles.standfirst: Raphinha casi cuadruplica (con 19) los goles que suman los tres delanteros del Atlético: Jonathan David (3), Julián (2) y Sorloth (0).
articles.summary: Raphinha casi cuadruplica (con 19) los goles que suman los tres delanteros del Atlético: Jonathan David (3), Julián (2) y Sorloth (0).
articles.body: Duelo de delanteros centro en el Metropolitano. Duelo que, al menos antes de rodar el esférico, está claramente decantado por el equipo que, sobre el papel, carecía de la figura del cazagoles tras las salidas el pasado verano de Lewandowski y Ferran, encargados de mandar a la jaula los balones azulgrana el último curso. Pues bien, cuando se han disputado 15 encuentros entre Liga y Champions el rendimiento goleador de Atlético y Barça dista mucho de ser equilibrado. Los de Flick, que se ha inventado a un panzer en la figura de Raphinha, ganan la partida 19-5. Sí, 19 goles lleva sólo el brasileño... por los 5 que suman entre los tres delanteros centros con los que cuenta Simeone. Jonathan David, con 3, lidera el particular pulso goleador de los 9. Julián, con 2, le secunda. Sorloth, todavía sin estrenarse, es el tercero en discordia aunque ante el Bayern empezó en el once titular. Cinco goles entre los tres que es casi la cuarta parte que los que lleva solo un Raphinha que tiene en Simeone uno de sus mayores admiradores, como reconoció públicamente al 'pedir' para él el Balón de Oro que acabó en la vitrina del jugador del PSG, Dembelé. Aunque no es tan sonrojante la comparativa, el hecho de que un jugador que no es delantero centro como Baena lleve los mismos goles, 5, que los tres encargados de ajusticiar a los rivales es cuanto menos sorprendente. El 10 está siendo, quizá junto a Oblak, el más regular de los rojiblancos y será una de las amenazas mientras los Julián y Cía. recuperan su mejor nivel. En el pasado, de hecho, los tres delanteros centros del Atlético han demostrado que pueden superar los 20 goles por curso. Una cifra considerable que está cerca de alcanzar ya Raphinha cuando el calendario apenas acaba de recibir noviembre y apenas se han disputado 15 choques oficiales. La importancia del actual 9 azulgrana se reflejó a la perfección en los elogios de Simeone en su comparecencia previa. "Para mí es un futbolista extraordinario. Con trabajo, con gol, con asistencias... Ha comenzado de una manera brillante en una posición diferente", deslizó el técnico sobre el delantero más efectivo de la temporada. El del 19-5.

articles.title: Did Lionel Messi never forgive PSG? Argentine spotted with personalised bag featuring every club he has played for except French giants
articles.summary: Lionel Messi was recently spotted with a custom bag featuring crests of all clubs he's played for, excluding Paris Saint-Germain. The absence has sparked speculation about his relationship with the French club after a turbulent two seasons.
articles.body: Lionel Messi has never been particularly short of reminders of the clubs and teams that have shaped his career, but a recent photograph has given supporters something unexpected to examine. The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner was spotted arriving at Inter Miami's training facilities carrying a personalised black bag decorated with several football crests. Barcelona, Newell's Old Boys, Inter Miami and Argentina were all represented, but one club from his playing history was nowhere to be seen: Paris Saint-Germain.The four crests on Messi's bag and the club missing from the collectionThe photograph, shared by Inter Miami, quickly attracted attention after supporters noticed the selection of badges on Messi's personalised mate-drinking bag. The black accessory features the crests of Barcelona, Newell's Old Boys, Inter Miami and the Argentina national team, representing different stages of a career that has taken him from Rosario to the highest levels of European and international football.The absence of PSG was particularly noticeable because Messi spent two seasons with the French club between 2021 and 2023. His time in Paris was a significant chapter in his career, even if it never developed into the kind of lasting attachment he had established with Barcelona.The photographs prompted discussion across social media, with some supporters interpreting the missing crest as a deliberate snub to the Parisian club. Messi, however, has not explained the selection or indicated whether the omission carries any particular meaning. There is consequently no confirmation that the missing badge was intended as a message to PSG, rather than simply a personal choice about which crests to include.The other four symbols have clear connections to his footballing journey. Newell's Old Boys were the club where Messi developed as a young player in Argentina, Barcelona became the institution with which he is most closely associated, Argentina represents his international career, and Inter Miami is the club he joined after leaving European football in 2023.What happened during Messi's two years at PSG?Messi's absence from the bag has attracted attention partly because his departure from Paris followed a difficult period in which his relationship with the club's supporters and hierarchy deteriorated. He joined PSG in August 2021 after Barcelona's financial crisis and La Liga's salary regulations prevented the Catalan club from registering a contract extension, despite both Messi and Barcelona wanting to continue their partnership.His arrival alongside Neymar and Kylian Mbappé generated enormous expectations, with PSG hoping the attacking trio would finally deliver the Champions League trophy. Messi produced impressive individual numbers, recording 32 goals and 34 assists in 75 appearances across his two seasons. He also helped the club secure two Ligue 1 titles and the 2022 Trophée des Champions. However, domestic success was not enough to satisfy supporters whose primary ambition remained European glory.PSG's consecutive Champions League round-of-16 exits proved particularly damaging. Messi and Neymar increasingly became scapegoats for the team's European failures, with sections of the club's ultras directing boos and whistles towards the two forwards. The atmosphere surrounding Messi became even more complicated following Argentina's triumph over France in the 2022 World Cup final in Qatar. Despite returning to Paris as a world champion, Messi experienced a noticeable shift in the reception from sections of the Parc des Princes crowd. He later acknowledged that the way he was treated changed considerably after the tournament, particularly following Argentina's victory over the host nation.His personal adjustment to life in Paris also proved difficult. Messi had not wanted to leave Barcelona and struggled to establish the same sense of belonging he had enjoyed in Spain. He openly discussed his difficulties adapting to his new surroundings, with the challenges extending into family life. He even mentioned how restrictions and complaints from neighbours, including concerns about his children playing football in the garden, made settling in more complicated.The relationship with PSG's management reached its breaking point in May 2023. Following a defeat, Messi travelled to Saudi Arabia to fulfil an existing promotional commitment as a tourism ambassador. The club had reportedly changed its training schedule at short notice, meaning the trip resulted in him missing a scheduled session. PSG responded by imposing a two-week suspension, suspending his salary payments during that period and taking disciplinary action against the Argentine. Messi subsequently issued a public video apology, but the incident further damaged an already strained relationship and effectively ended hopes of a contract renewal.After his departure, Messi also expressed disappointment that PSG had not officially celebrated his 2022 World Cup triumph, particularly as he was the only member of Argentina's victorious squad playing for the French club. PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi later criticised the forward for speaking negatively about the club after leaving, demonstrating that tensions had continued beyond his departure.Messi eventually left when his contract expired in the summer of 2023, joining Inter Miami rather than continuing his European career. Neymar, who also departed PSG that summer, subsequently reflected on their final period in Paris as an unhappy experience, describing how the two friends had felt isolated and unappreciated despite their contributions. Their experiences helped explain why Messi's apparent omission of PSG from his personalised bag has attracted attention, although he has not publicly suggested that leaving out the French club's crest was a deliberate snub.From Newell's Old Boys to Barcelona, Argentina and Inter MiamiThe four crests displayed on Messi's bag trace a career that began long before his arrival in Paris. Born in Rosario, Argentina, he first played football for Abanderado Grandoli, a neighbourhood club where his father helped coach him. At six, he joined Newell's Old Boys, developing in the youth side famously known as The Machine of '87, where he established himself as one of the most promising young players in the region.His move to Barcelona came in 2000, when he was 13, after the Spanish club agreed to bring him into its academy, La Masia. He made his first-team debut in October 2004, aged 17, and went on to spend 17 senior seasons at the club. During that period, he became Barcelona's record goalscorer, won multiple domestic and European honours and established himself as one of the defining players in the history of the game.His departure in 2021 was driven by Barcelona's financial situation rather than a sporting decision to move elsewhere. After two seasons at PSG, Messi chose Inter Miami, joining the Major League Soccer club in July 2023 and beginning a new chapter in the United States.Argentina, meanwhile, remains central to his career. After years of international disappointment, Messi captained the national team to victory at the 2022 World Cup, completing the major achievement that had eluded him for much of his career.The bag's selection of crests therefore brings together four distinct parts of Messi's footballing life, from his childhood in Rosario to his present at Inter Miami. PSG, despite its two seasons and the trophies won there, is absent. Whether that was intentional remains unknown, but given how his time in Paris ended, the missing badge was always likely to attract attention.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: El Racing por fin rompía su racha negativa a domicilio a lo grande, sumando los tres puntos ante el Málaga, un rival directo por mantener la categoría
articles.body: José Alberto valoraba el partido ante el Málaga, ' Ha sido una victoria de equipo muy trabajada. La 1ª parte ha sido igualada, en la 2ª parte hemos entrado muy bien para dar la vuelta el marcador. Desde la expulsión de ellos no hemos gestionado bien el resultado'. El técnico asturiano se queda con lo positivo del partido, ' Me ha gustado hasta la superioridad numérica, pudimos matar el partido pero no hemos tenido control sobre el partido. El Málaga en el tramo final tuvo sus opciones'. José Alberto reconocía que es un alivio ganar fuera fuera, 'Conseguir ganar en 1ª en difícil, sabía que iba a ser un encuentro complicado. Cuando no ganas fuera se te hace bola pero nos hemos quitado una losa'. El entrenador racinguista estaba feliz por el inicio segundo tiempo, ' Hemos hecho 20 o 25 minutos del segundo tiempo muy bueno. Si no podemos marcar el tercero tenemos que tener más calma'. José Alberto valoraba la actuación de Pablo García e Iker Luque, ' Los dos han estado muy bien, Iker ha hecho muy buen partido nos da agresividad y Pablo también netró bien en el segundo periodo'. El Racing llega a este parón liguero fuera de los puestos de descenso que era objetivo en el inicio de campaña.

articles.title: La Rosaleda pidió la dimisión de Loren Juarros
articles.standfirst: El Málaga lleva doce jornadas sin ganar
articles.summary: El Málaga lleva doce jornadas sin ganar
articles.body: La derrota ante el Racing de Santander (1-2) dejó una lectura bastante clara en La Rosaleda. La afición del Málaga CF no cargó contra Juanfran Funes, que no recibió pitos durante el encuentro, pero sí dirigió buena parte de su enfado hacia Loren Juarros. El director deportivo fue uno de los señalados en una tarde que volvió a dejar al malaguismo preocupado por el rumbo del equipo. Los cánticos contra Juarros se escucharon desde distintos sectores del estadio, aunque fue la Grada de Animación la que más insistió en las protestas contra el burgalés. También hubo algunas referencias a José María Muñoz, administrador judicial del club, si bien con bastante menos intensidad. La grada pareció tener claro dónde poner el foco de su descontento: Funes salió indemne de la protesta, mientras que Loren volvió a quedar en el punto de mira. El resultado no hace más que aumentar la preocupación alrededor de un proyecto deportivo que no termina de arrancar. La planificación de la plantilla, cuestionada ya públicamente por Manuel Pellegrini en la anterior jornada, volvió a estar en el centro del debate. Esta vez, además, con una parte de La Rosaleda señalando directamente a uno de los principales responsables de la parcela deportiva. En el césped, el Málaga volvió a tropezar en un partido de máxima necesidad. El Racing se llevó los tres puntos y agravó la situación de los blanquiazules, que siguen sin encontrar la respuesta necesaria para salir de la zona baja. El equipo de Funes volvió a pagar sus errores y se quedó sin premio ante un rival que supo aprovechar mejor sus ocasiones.

articles.title: La rajada de Dotor tras una nueva derrota del colista: "Hicimos 20' inaceptables, toca mirarnos a la cara y decirnos las cosas"
articles.standfirst: El goleador del Málaga habla claro tras una nueva derrota
articles.summary: El goleador del Málaga habla claro tras una nueva derrota
articles.body: Dotor, jugador del Málaga y goleador del equipo local, habló claro después del partido. El futbolista reconoció el mal momento del conjunto y reclamó una reacción colectiva para corregir los errores que están penalizando al equipo. “Es un momento difícil para todos. No están saliendo las cosas como queremos. Hemos hecho unos 20 minutos en la segunda parte que son inaceptables. Hay que apretar todos. Mirarnos a las caras, decirnos las cosas y seguir hacia adelante”, aseguró. El centrocampista insistió en la necesidad de elevar la exigencia y evitar desconexiones como la sufrida tras el descanso. Su mensaje apuntó al compromiso de todos para recuperar el rumbo y volver a ganar partidos. “Lo mínimo que podemos hacer es darlo todo. Pero no podemos regalar los primeros minutos de la segunda parte. Tenemos que hacernos mirar eso. Si queremos seguir y ganar partidos, tenemos que apretar todos”, comentó. Dotor también valoró la acción en la que reclamó una llegada tardía del guardameta rival. “Lo que he visto es que voy a rematar y el portero llega tarde. Creo que es una acción peligrosa, pero bueno, no la he visto repetida”, comentó.

articles.summary: El técnico del Málaga lamentó el mal inicio de segunda mitad
articles.body: Juanfran Funes se mostró triste tras la derrota ante el Racing y aseguró que siempre va a estar del lado del club. El técnico queda en una situación muy delicada tras una nueva derrota y después de no conocer la victoria tras doce jornadas disputadas. Partido: "Ese inicio de la segunda parte ha sido muy malo, Pablo (García) nos ha hecho mucho daño, nos hundieron el bloque y ha llegado su remontada. Bajón en la segunda parte: "Veníamos de hacer una buena primera mitad, no somos capaces de cerrar el partido, incluso con una ocasión al inicio de la segunda parte. El castigo es grande. Luego en el tramo final con mucha casta y mucho empuje, pero con mucha dificultad". Futuro: "Hoy es un día difícil para nosotros. Hay que reflexionar, pensar todo bien. Tenemos que asumir la responsabilidad. Siempre estoy al lado del club, al servicio del club. Las circunstancias que vengan las afrontamos siempre".

articles.title: Pólvora mojada en Nervión
articles.standfirst: El Sevilla empata con el Alavés y se queda sin marcar por primera vez este curso, marchándose al parón con la necesidad de recuperar una mejor versión
articles.summary: El Sevilla empata con el Alavés y se queda sin marcar por primera vez este curso, marchándose al parón con la necesidad de recuperar una mejor versión
articles.body: En una noche marcada por los homenajes a Jesús de Miguel, Sevilla y Alavés protagonizaron un partido con rigor táctico y escasa brillantez en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán. Los locales estuvieron más cerca del triunfo, pero esta vez el dominio posicional y el juego directo no se tradujo en goles. Ni siquiera un penalti a favor les valió para superar a Antonio Sivera, que se convirtió en el mejor futbolista del encuentro (0-0). Al equipo de Nervión se le mojó la pólvora coincidiendo con su peor momento en lo que va de curso. El empate deja otro regusto amargo antes de marcharse al parón con la mente ya puesta en el Gran Derbi. Luis García Plaza realizó dos modificaciones respecto al once inicial del Coliseum, manteniendo a Isaac como segundo delantero en el 4-2-3-1. En primer lugar, decidió dar descanso a Castrín para alinear a Sangante, que no jugaba en Liga desde la séptima jornada ante el Barcelona -curiosamente antes del parón de selecciones-; en segundo, apostó por Rubén Vargas en banda derecha en vez de Ejuke, al que quería tener fresco de cara a la segunda parte. Un esquema muy definido pensando también en un encuentro que debía cocerse a fuego lento. El partido arrancó con un ritmo alto en los primeros instantes, pues apenas hubo interrupciones más allá del segundo homenaje a Jesús de Miguel en el minuto 9. Al principio, el Alavés pudo jugar mucho tiempo en campo contrario enviando centros laterales al área del Sevilla. Por su parte, el cuadro hispalense atacó los espacios que dejaba la defensa babazorra. Isaac se acercaba con frecuencia a las bandas, sobre todo a la izquierda, donde protagonizó un intenso duelo con Tenaglia. A partir del minuto 20, el Sevilla se hizo con el dominio de la posesión y embotelló al Alavés. En este contexto emergió la figura de Stassin, que mejoraba todas las jugadas que pasaban por él al detectar el pase al compañero antes de que le llegara el balón. Pese a su buena primera mitad, al delantero belga todavía le falta tener más maldad en zonas de peligro para ponerse de cara a gol. Ambos equipos realizaron muy pocas concesiones, ya fuera por méritos de los defensas o deméritos de los atacantes. Una vez más, los mejores ataques del Sevilla nacieron desde la banda izquierda, donde Suazo y Félix Correia se juntaron con Isaac y con Vargas. El extremo portugués, siempre generoso en las ayudas defensivas, provocó un penalti de jugador avispado. Aprovechando que Ángel Pérez plantó la pierna tras su recorte, forzó el contacto en una jugada en la que el VAR -esta vez sí- no debía intervenir. Una lástima que no sirviera para adelantar a los sevillistas porque fue de largo el que más lo intentó en ataque. La sociedad formada por Suazo y Félix es de lo mejor que tiene el Sevilla en este primer tercio del campeonato. El chileno merece una mención aparte por su regularidad, su crecimiento partido tras partido y el gran momento de confianza que atraviesa: gana todos los duelos, inicia desde atrás con buen criterio, oxigena el juego cuando es necesario, se proyecta por su carril hasta alcanzar línea de fondo, pone los mejores centros… incluso regatea rivales y lanza faltas directas. Está justificando su capitanía junto a un Kike Salas cuyo nivel ya no sorprende a nadie, aunque en esta ocasión estuvo poco certero en los pases. Con el paso de los minutos y el desgaste físico, especialmente de Félix, el fútbol del Sevilla se volvió espeso y previsible. Continuó creándole peligro al Alavés, pero lo hizo más por arreones que por lucidez. Prueba de ello fueron las únicas dos oportunidades claras, que estuvieron en las botas de Juan Iglesias. "Si tampoco los delanteros hacen goles, falta un jugador que a lo mejor sea capaz de cambiar el partido, y nos ha faltado estar acertados en las ocasiones que hemos tenido", argumentó Luis García Plaza. El bache de resultados del Sevilla se explica en buena medida mediante el bajón de rendimiento de Fofana, que otra vez dejó una actuación muy discreta. Algo más encorsetado por detrás de los dos delanteros, el francés acumula dos partidos seguidos en los que ni pisa área ni rompe líneas en conducción, algo que le había permitido a su equipo generar desajustes en los rivales en las primeras jornadas. Sin su aportación, a los suyos le cuesta un mundo progresar por el centro ante defensas cerradas. El debate sobre la posición ideal de Fofana fue uno de los temas centrales en la rueda de prensa posterior al choque. "Contra Osasuna me gustó mucho en el mediocentro y cuando le pusimos por delante en Getafe estuvo bastante flojo. Hoy no ha estado tan bien, pero confiamos en él", aseguró su entrenador, que debe aprovechar el parón para recuperar una mejor versión de su jugador más diferencial. El futbolista del Sevilla más señalado fue Vargas. El extremo suizo comenzó muy activo partiendo desde el flanco diestro para caer a zonas centrales. Sin embargo, tras fallar el penalti no se supo reenganchar al partido, siendo el primer sustituido y recibiendo pitos de la grada. En su lugar, Ejuke le dio algo más de vuelo a esa banda, aunque por ese perfil los zagueros suelen intuir bien sus regates hacia fuera, lo que le lleva a tomar peores decisiones en el último tercio del campo. Las otras soluciones de Luis García Plaza desde el banquillo fueron dar entrada a Castrín y Robbie Ure por Sangante e Isaac. De esta forma, el dibujo táctico ya sí fijaba un 4-4-2 más clásico con el escocés acompañando a Stassin en la doble punta, una fórmula que de momento no parece funcionar. Frente a un Alavés muy arropado y al que sostuvo un Sivera colosal, en la segunda parte el Sevilla solo halló el modo de atacar realizando cambios de orientación constantes para buscar a sus extremos con espacio por delante, metiendo centros al área visitante que casi nunca encontraban rematador. "Hemos sido muy merecedores de la victoria, pero esto se trata de marcar", opinó luego el técnico madrileño. Parón necesario El resultado gafas entre Sevilla y Alavés supone la primera vez que el conjunto blanquirrojo se queda sin poder marcar en esta temporada. En la parte positiva, sufrió poco atrás y recobró la confianza defensiva consiguiendo su cuarta portería a cero. Si bien es un empate que le sabe amargo, al menos suma un punto que le acerca cada vez más al objetivo de la permanencia. "Nos vamos en una situación buena, sabiendo que va a haber mucha igualdad en la Liga. Lo importante es no meterte en ese grupo de abajo y estar cuanto más arriba, mejor", comentó Luis García Plaza respecto a la inminente ventana de selecciones. Al igual que el anterior parón cortó de raíz la buena dinámica de su equipo, esta vez debe servirle para recuperar sensaciones, ya que la próxima cita será nada más y nada menos que el derbi sevillano.

articles.title: Truro City: Game at Folkestone Invicta abandoned after Yassine En-Neyah collapses
articles.summary: Saturday's National League South match between Folkestone Invicta and Truro City is postponed after a player collapses during the warm-up.
articles.body:
Saturday's match between Folkestone Invicta and Truro City was abandoned before kick-off after a player collapsed during the warm-up.

Truro City midfielder Yassine En-Neyah was taken ill shortly before the National League South game in Kent.

The 26-year-old joined Truro from Irish side Waterford in February 2023, having previously been on the books at Nottingham Forest.

He has scored one goal in 11 appearances for the Cornish side this season.

"Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment," a Truro statement read.

"We will provide a further update in due course."

Truro were second in the table before this afternoon's matches, with Folkestone in 15th place.

articles.body:
Roma are eyeing Barcelona for the January transfer window. And Tony D'Amico has Alejandro Balde in his sights.

The Spanish left-back could leave the Blaugrana as early as the next transfer window, and the Giallorossi want to capitalize on this.

According to Spanish newspaper SPORT , the sporting director has already met with Jorge Mendes, the player's agent, to determine whether there are opportunities to bring him to the capital.

Meanwhile, things are moving at Barcelona. Flick would like to strengthen the defense with a new center-back, but the club's financial difficulties would necessitate at least one departure.

And Balde, who has played just 124 minutes this season, is reportedly among the leading candidates to leave.

The Spanish club's asking price is around €40 million, although the possibility of a loan with an obligation to buy, subject to certain conditions, is gaining traction.

The road, however, is far from clear. In the Premier League, Liverpool, Aston Villa, and Manchester United are monitoring the situation, without having yet submitted official offers. Juventus has also set its sights on the full-back, but in Italy, Roma are reportedly keen to make a move.

Gasperini particularly appreciates the Spaniard's qualities, and D'Amico has reportedly already begun exploring the possibility of an agreement. The main issue, even more than the transfer fee, remains Balde's salary. Mendes is reportedly evaluating various options for his client, with a final decision expected in December. Roma, meanwhile, is waiting, ready to play its cards if the financial conditions for the deal to close are met.

articles.title: 'You still haven't seen the best version of me' - Bradley Barcola makes honest admission over slow start at Liverpool
articles.summary: Bradley Barcola has admitted that Liverpool supporters are yet to see the best of him following his big-money summer move from Paris Saint-Germain. The Frenc...
articles.body:
Bradley Barcola has admitted that Liverpool supporters are yet to see the best of him following his big-money summer move from Paris Saint-Germain. The French forward has struggled for consistency since arriving at Anfield, with all three of his goals coming in one game, but insists things are improving all the time as his new team-mates learn how to make the most of his strengths.

Barcola admits he is not yet at his best for Liverpool

Barcola joined the Reds for £123 million from Champions League holders PSG in a deal many saw as a major coup. However, he has struggled to impress regularly so far, with all three of his goals for the club coming in the 6-3 win away to LASK.

Speaking to the Liverpool Echo, Barcola conceded that he is still finding his feet in England. "No, I don't think I'm at my best yet," he said. "You still haven't seen the best version of me. On top of that, we're working with my team-mates so that they can make the most of my strengths."

Barcola confident understanding with team-mates will grow

The 24-year-old believes his best form will follow once he and his new colleagues are fully on the same wavelength, and he insists there are already clear signs of progress during his early months in the Premier League.

"So yes, I think once we really develop that understanding, things will get much better," Barcola continued. "And I think things are improving all the time. People are beginning to understand my style of play much better. I think it's going much better."

Barcola explains why it was the right time to leave PSG

Barcola made the big decision to depart PSG in order to be a regular starter at Liverpool, and he opened up on opting for a new challenge. "For me, it was the right time to leave PSG," he added. "I spent so many great years there and I won an enormous amount of trophies. But it was time. It was quite difficult because, over there, it was a real family. We'd built something very special together.

"On top of that, it was very difficult to leave and say goodbye to my team-mates. But ultimately, that's just how football is. Ever since I was young, I always had the ambition of playing in the Premier League. When a club like Liverpool comes calling, it's a great thing. I didn't have any doubts and I just knew I had to come here. I'm happy to be here, and I hope things go well for PSG."

Liverpool will need far more from Barcola to justify his £123m fee, in terms of both end product and all-round influence. So far, he has been reluctant to run at defenders and use his blistering pace, which points to a lack of confidence.

Barcola is also yet to link up seamlessly with his team-mates, and the Reds will hope the understanding he speaks of arrives sooner rather than later.

articles.title: Okafor sinks Spurs after Leeds survive major VAR scare
articles.summary: Leeds survived a major VAR controversy against Tottenham on Saturday before striking late through substitute Noah Okafor to end the visitors' winning run.Lee...
articles.body:
Leeds survived a major VAR controversy against Tottenham on Saturday before striking late through substitute Noah Okafor to end the visitors' winning run.

Swiss winger Okafor scored 97 seconds after being introduced late in the game as the home side were rewarded for an impressive second-half performance.

The major talking point in the first period was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team's second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident after the game, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks.

"In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing," he told TNT Sports.

He added: "I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn't take the right decision, I don't know, but we have confidence."

Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road on the back of three straight wins after a shocking start to the season left them bottom of the Premier League.

Leeds, on the eve of the international break, have snapped a five-match winless run and climbed to eighth in the table ahead of the later matches on Saturday.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke said his team had shown "great spirit, great commitment, great unity today", adding that they were deserving winners.

The home side started brightly and Spurs breathed a sigh of relief in the early minutes when VAR ruled that Mateus Fernandes had not handled the ball in the penalty area.

As the first half wore on the visitors established themselves, though clear chances were at a premium.

Tel was caught on the ankle by the studs of Bogle in the 34th minute, leading to a VAR check of more than four minutes.

But the referee's original decision stood after it was deemed there was a lack of speed going into the tackle and Bogle escaped without even a yellow card.

Minutes later Tel had to leave the field, replaced by Dominic Solanke.

Leeds started the second half on the front foot and created a number of good chances -- Dominic Calvert-Lewin's header was blocked before Ao Tanaka blasted over the bar.

Goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky produced a wonderful fingertip save after Sean Longstaff's swivel and shot as pressure mounted on lacklustre Spurs.

Leeds finally got the reward their pressure deserved in the 79th minute, when Okafor lashed past the helpless Kinsky after combining with fellow substitute Harry Wilson.

Spurs came agonisingly close to an equaliser in stoppage time but James Trafford made a brilliant save to keep out Jan Paul van Hecke's header.

articles.title: El Bayern se apoya en el Kane más generoso
articles.standfirst: El ariete inglés repartió las dos asistencias del triunfo contra el Mainz
articles.summary: El ariete inglés repartió las dos asistencias del triunfo contra el Mainz
articles.body: A Harry Kane se le sigue resistiendo el gol desde que fue condecorado como Balón de Oro. Sin embargo, está sacando a relucir una versión todavía más generosa de lo habitual. Asistió en 'Der Klassiker', repitió en el Metropolitano... y sirvió las dos del triunfo del Bayern en su visita al Mainz (1-2). Con Kompany todavía ausente, Aaron Danks realizó varios ajustes respecto al once que venía de imponerse al Atlético de Madrid en Champions. Pavlovic recuperó su sitio junto a Kimmich en la sala de máquinas, mientras que 'Nene' Brown se ubicó en la mediapunta junto a Olise y Karl. No transmitía la sensación el Bayern de haber saltado demasiado entonado al césped. En su primer acercamiento, sin embargo, Kimmich comenzó a inclinar el marcador. El Mainz perdió el balón a la altura del medio campo con el equipo desplegado, Kane levantó la cabeza en tres cuartos y habilitó la llegada desde segunda línea del alemán, que soltó un 'latigazo' inapelable. El Bayern se fue haciendo con el control de la situación y rebajó el nivel de intensidad con el que había entrado al partido el Mainz. A poco más de cinco minutos para el descanso, eso sí, tuvo que intervenir el VAR para anular un tanto de Jae-sung Lee a balón parado. Se salvó de salir en otra foto delicada un Manuel Neuer que, sin embargo, tuvo que dejarle su sitio a Urbig después de volver a sufrir molestias en el pie. Se había llevado un buen susto el Bayern antes de poner rumbo al túnel de vestuarios. Sin embargo, antes de alcanzar a la hora de partido, Laimer encontró a Harry Kane en el interior del área y firmó su segunda asistencia de la tarde en favor de un Lennart Karl que venía de marcar en el Metropolitano. Sigue reivindicándose tras recibir algún que otro toque de atención. Fue curioso, cuanto menos, que Aaron Danks diese entrada a Bischof y Davies al mismo tiempo con más de 20' por delante... y fuese el internacional alemán quien se ubicase como lateral izquierdo. Todo ello, con 'Nene' Brown todavía en el terreno de juego. El propio Davies y Upamecano pudieron terminar de resolver el choque para un Bayern que midió bastante sus esfuerzos tras el desgaste del Metropolitano. Tietz recortó distancias en el descuento a centro de Hollerbach tras ganarle la posición a Tah. Llegó, sin embargo, demasiado tarde para el Mainz. El Borussia Dortmund sigue aguantando el tirón del Bayern cuando ya se ha alcanzado la jornada nueve da la Bundesliga. Los de Niko Kovac, que venían de sacar un agónico empate en 'Der Klassiker' disputado en el Allianz la semana pasada, lograron imponerse al Elversberg (2-0) para mantener el coliderato antes de afrontar el segundo parón del curso. Fue Félix Nmecha el encargado de amarrar el triunfo anotando un doblete durante la segunda mitad. Escasos 10' después de regresar del descanso, lució golpeo desde la frontal a pase de Fábio Silva. Todavía mejor, sin embargo, fue el 'cañonazo' que se inventó en el 71' para duplicar la ventaja. Tuvieron que acabar sufriendo, eso sí, con el tanto de 'tijereta' de Futkeu a menos de 10' para el final. Celebraba Ole Book, ex director deportivo del Elversberg, tras finalizar el choque.

articles.title: Leeds 1-0 Tottenham: Tottenham set to complain to Pro Ref - but should Bogle have seen red?
articles.summary: Tottenham are set to submit a formal complaint about the decision not to send off Jayden Bogle for his challenge on Mathys Tel during the defeat by Leeds.
articles.body:
Tottenham are set to submit a formal complaint about the decision not to send off Jayden Bogle for his challenge on Mathys Tel during the defeat by Leeds .

Bogle, 26, escaped any punishment despite catching Spurs forward Tel on the back of the ankle with his studs in the first half of Saturday's game.

It is understood Tottenham believe Bogle should have been sent off and will write to refereeing body Pro Ref to seek an explanation as to why the incident did not result in a dismissal.

The challenge was reviewed thoroughly by the Video Assistant Referee (VAR), but referee John Brooks was not sent to the pitch-side monitor, meaning Bogle escaped any punishment.

Former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann said the Leeds defender was "fortunate" not to be dismissed.

"Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent," Cann told BBC Sport. "He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch."

By the time play resumed, there were less than nine minutes of the first half remaining and Tottenham 's momentum - and composure - were fading quickly.

Roberto de Zerbi's side never appeared to recover from the incident and, after the break, were outworked and outplayed by the home side.

Nevertheless, the Italian - perhaps buoyed by his side's recent rise up the table - refused to pinpoint Spurs ' failings on the referee's decision.

"We deserved to lose the game in the second half and didn't play like we can," he told TNT Sports. "It's a journey for us because we can learn from this game.

"I am sorry for the performance in the second half - we didn't play like a top team. We didn't have the right character and physicality in the second half."

Okafor downs Tottenham to earn Leeds first win since September

Okafor the difference despite Van Hecke defiance - Leeds v Spurs ratings

'We have full confidence in the referee and VAR'

When the PA system at Elland Road confirmed there was a VAR check in progress, it seemed only a matter of time before Bogle would be shown a red card.

The Leeds defender was full-blooded in his pursuit of the ball from Tel and seemed certain to follow in the footsteps of Crystal Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta, who was sent off for a similar challenge against Spurs last weekend.

What was strange about the situation, though, was that at no point did Brooks make his way to the pitchside monitor to review the incident.

It meant the entire four-minute review was conducted solely by those in the VAR hub at Stockley Park.

"They've said no red card, and this will create debate," former Tottenham midfielder Michael Brown told BBC Radio 5 Live.

And because Brooks had not initially cautioned Bogle, the defender escaped the incident without any punishment.

"I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor," said De Zerbi. "If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve."

Early in the second half, Tottenham 's frustration - seemingly stemming from the decision not to dismiss Bogle - came to a head when defender Pedro Porro and De Zerbi himself were booked simultaneously following a challenge by the Spanish defender.

De Zerbi described the decision to caution Porro as "incredible" after what had transpired during the first half.

"I was surprised on the yellow card for Pedro Porro because it was clear," the Italian told BBC Match of the Day. "The potential red card, I couldn't say.

"We have full confidence in the referee and VAR. I cannot say nothing more."

Was Bogle fortunate to escape a red card?

Bogle was certainly very lucky to escape even a booking.

The foul happened in strange circumstances. Bogle was positioning his body to challenge Tel with his right foot, and in trying to plant his left foot he stood on the ankle of the Spurs player.

At full speed it looked innocuous, which is probably why referee Brooks chose not to show a card after giving the foul.

Once the slow-motion replays were looked at it became apparent that the nature of the contact on Tel was very ugly, with the twist of the ankle.

It could easily have resulted in the VAR, Tony Harrington, sending Brooks to the pitchside monitor for an on-field review for a red card.

Harrington spent far too long looking at the replays, probably feeling he had more time while Tel received treatment. But longer reviews only tend to cause doubts about process.

Harrington eventually told Brooks: "I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There's a lack of speed going into the challenge and he's stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge."

A reckless challenge is a yellow card, but the VAR is unable to intervene and advise that Bogle should be booked.

Something else Harrington said is important - "stepping into the challenge".

It does not mean a player cannot be sent off, but this is far less likely to result in a VAR review for a red card because such challenges naturally come with less force.

How about comparisons with Mateta's VAR red card against Spurs last week?

There is an argument that Mateta, who was booked on-field, made less forceful contact on the ankle of Micky van de Ven. Yet it is the nature of the challenge that is crucially different.

Mateta made a lunging, stretching tackle with studs leading, the kind generally considered to come with a higher degree of force and potential danger to the opponent.

That said, and even though Bogle was not really making a challenge, the nature of the contact means many may feel there should have been a VAR review for a red card.

articles.title: Mucho Leo para Eder
articles.standfirst: El meta del Deportivo evita con sus paradas el triunfo del Espanyol en el primer el encuentro del técnico. Buena primera parte del equipo perico, al que ya se le notó la mano de Sarabia
articles.summary: El meta del Deportivo evita con sus paradas el triunfo del Espanyol en el primer el encuentro del técnico. Buena primera parte del equipo perico, al que ya se le notó la mano de Sarabia
articles.body: El 'efecto Sarabia' se notó, pero se quedó a medias. El Espanyol, que dio buena imagen, sobre todo en el primer tiempo, no pudo con el Dépor en el estreno del nuevo técnico perico, que no estuvo en el banquillo al tener que cumplir sanción. Aunque no ganó, Eder se llevó un punto y ahora tendrá tiempo en el parón para impregnar sus ideas, esas que ya se vieron en el RCDE Stadium en el equipo catalán. Sarabia se topó con un problema: el portero Leo Román, que se redimió de su error ante Osasuna. El Espanyol mostró las señas de identidad de Eder desde el inicio. Un equipo atrevido, con toque, posesión y una idea clara: atacar. Roberto Fernández tuvo las dos primeras ocasiones del encuentro al poco de empezar. Una, en el minuto 9, la salvó Giménez, providencial al lanzarse en el área y tapar el remate. Y otra, justo después, la desbarató Leo Román con una mano abajo fantástica para desviar el cabezazo del delantero a pase de El Hilali. Fue la primera intervención del portero del Deportivo, que sujetó a los gallegos en los peores momentos. Más tarde voló para poner un guante de cemento y detener un cabezazo de Alejandro Santiago. Qué parada, por Dios. Si no la han visto, por favor, véanla. Disfrutaba la grada del RCDE Stadium y sufría el Dépor, que también encontraba su hueco para asustar a los pericos. Amatucci, que recogió un buen balón filtrado, superó con una picadita la salida de Fortuño, pero apareció El Hilali, bien en ataque y bien en defensa, para evitar el tanto. Los gallegos dieron un paso adelante y, al filo de la media hora, Luismi Cruz lo intentó con un disparo desde la frontal que salió desviado. Fue un espejismo, porque el Espanyol, rondando el 70% de posesión, volvió a mandar. A los pericos sólo les faltó acertar en el primer tiempo. Hidalgo tomó cartas en el asunto en el descanso. Al campo Aubameyang y Villares, fuera Yeremay y Luismi Cruz. Buena decisión del míster, que permitió a los gallegos oponer mayor resistencia al Espanyol. El partido entró en una fase más trabada. Pero ambicioso, el técnico del Dépor introdujo más pólvora en el campo. El momento de Traoré llegó en el 61'. A diferencia de la primera mitad, el encuentro transcurría sin ocasiones, más allá de un susto que le dio Auba a Fortuño. El meta se hizo un lío al golpear el balón, pero salió ileso del sobresalto. Eder también movió piezas y entró Javi Hernández, otro agitador. Ni por esas. Y en la única acción de peligro, ya en el 90', volvió a aparecer Leo Román para negar el gol a Roberto Fernández. Qué partido del portero.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Man City: Liam Delap ends City Ground goal drought as City lose three on the bounce
articles.summary: Match report and free highlights as Nottingham Forest ended their City Ground goal drought with a 3-1 win over Manchester City in which Liam Delap scored twice after Jair Cunha’s opener. Forest out of the relegation zone. City now six points behind Arsenal
articles.body:
City had suffered back-to-back Premier League defeats but few could have expected Oliver Glasner's side to expose them this emphatically given that Forest were goalless let alone winless at home this season. Instead, their intensity was too much for City.

Forest fans had to wait almost six months and watch eight-and-a-half hours of football here without seeing their side score, but it was a stunner when it came. Jair Cunha tracked Josko Gvardiol, dispossessed him and ran through to score with his left foot.

That came in the sixth minute but Glasner's side were two up 12 minutes later, this time Xaver Schlager beating former Forest man Elliot Anderson to the ball in midfield and sending the powerhouse Delap through to lash in just his second goal for the club.

City looked stunned at that point and James McAtee, playing in an advanced role with crowd favourite Ryan Yates brought in for this first start of the season, might have made it three before Enzo Maresca's men had offered anything. But there were then openings.

Enzo Fernandez should have headed in Marc Guehi's cross. Erling Haaland rounded Matz Sels only to see that man Jair Cunha clear his goal-bound shot. But by that stage Forest had a two-goal lead to hang onto in front of watching owner Evangelos Marinakis.

Rayan Cherki halved it early in the second half with a rocket of a shot and City did push for the equaliser but Morgan Gibbs-White fed Delap on the break and his angled shot found the top corner of the net to send the City Ground wild with delight - and relief.

This long-awaited win pulls them out of the drop zone and feels like a turning point for Glasner after his recent frustrations. For City, they are the first top-flight team in 122 years to win their first seven and lose the next three. They stay six points behind Arsenal.

Glasner: I had to run more than Maresca!

While his Forest players outran City on the pitch, Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner joked in the press conference that he had to do the same off it, referencing his touchline celebration for his team's third goal.

"I had to run more than Enzo Maresca as well and I did my job."

Asked how he felt when storming down the line, Glasner replied: "Very fast!"

There was praise too for Yates, who he credited with making an inspirational team-talk before kick-off.

"I have played more than 500 games as a player. I have managed more than 500 games as a manager. I have never heard such an inspiring speech to the team."

But when asked if this win would be a turning point for his team, he added: "We have a saying in Austria. One swallow does not make a summer."

Maresca: We didn't match their intensity

Man City head coach Enzo Maresca speaking in the press conference:

"It is quite clear that the first half was not good enough. We didn't match the intensity that these kind of games required. We conceded one, we conceded two and then we tried to react. In the second half we started much, much better. We scored one, we didn't score any more.

"Today we didn't match the intensity, we need to understand the reasons why.

"The second and the third goal that we conceded in transition, they are copy and paste. The second one, we lost the duel in the middle of the pitch, and the third one, we lost the duel at the edge of the box. And from there, as I said, if you make a mistake or you don't win duels, you can concede on transition."

Glasner had suggested after the loss to Brentford that the time had come to make changes. As it was, only two players came into the team for this game but one of them was particularly significant with skipper Yates making his first start of the season.

The popular midfielder personified the intensity required against City, not allowing them any time on the ball and also conducting the crowd in the rare moments when the noise levels dropped. He even helped spark the counter-attack for the dramatic third goal.

Delap was the player of the match but Yates symbolises the spirit that supporters have wanted to see from their side throughout this barren run. The celebrations upon the final whistle made this feel like a big moment. Typical that Yates should be part of it.

The question that Manchester City supporters might be asking right now is whether Yates and Xaver Schlager nipping at heels and Jair Cunha pressing up the pitch should have been enough for their side to unravel as they did. Three defeats in a row tells a tale.

Gvardiol was dispossessed for the first goal, Anderson was too weak for the second and Marc Guehi made it too easy as well. City look like a side who want to be allowed to play their football but when teams refuse to give them that time then they become unsettled.

Seven wins in a row to start the season suggested that, for all the issues engulfing City right now, it would be a seamless transition under Enzo Maresca on the pitch. But the blueprint for stopping them is now becoming clear. And that should be a major concern.

articles.title: Arsenal 1-0 Hull City: Another 1-0 for relentless Arsenal - but did Martin Odegaard spare VAR blushes?
articles.summary: Arsenal move six points clear at the top of the Premier League after beating Hull City - but did Martin Odegaard's goal save the blushes of the VAR?
articles.body:
It was not pretty, but Martin Odegaard's goal was enough to secure the 1-0 win that ensured Arsenal go into the international break as the Premier League leaders.

It was Arsenal's 34th 1-0 win under Mikel Arteta, to equal their best start to a Premier League season under the Spaniard of 27 points earned after 10 games in 2022-23.

No team has enjoyed more 1-0 wins since Arteta was appointed back in 2019, with the Gunners winning their past 10 home games in all competitions, keeping eight clean sheets in that time.

Odegaard's goal though, bundled home from close range, may well have been a relief to those at Pro Ref, too.

A controversial video assistant referee (VAR) decision, which denied the Gunners a first-half penalty, threatened to be the story as a largely uneventful game drifted by.

When referee Farai Hallam was sent to the pitchside monitor for a VAR review for a shirt pull by Nobel Mendy on Kai Havertz, surely everyone inside the Emirates was expecting a penalty.

The irony would not be lost on Liverpool fans, who were denied a VAR penalty for a shirt pull last weekend when Arsenal 's Jurrien Timber tugged back Alexander Isak.

Unlike Isak, Havertz made sure everyone - including VAR Michael Oliver, was aware that a defender had hold of his shirt.

Indeed, the cheers had already begun when Hallam started to describe the foul to the crowd - but Gunners supporters were stopped in their tracks. The referee pivoted to an offside against Havertz, and play restarted with a free-kick to Hull .

Had Arsenal not mustered that 72nd-minute winner from their captain, much of the attention would, once again, have been on VAR.

Tottenham set to complain to Pro Ref - but should Bogle have seen red?

Odegaard hits winner as Arsenal beat Hull to extend lead at top

If Arsenal had dropped points, it wouldn't have been the first time this weekend that a match would have been dominated by discussions about the video officials.

On Friday, Coventry City were denied what appeared to be a clear penalty against Everton for a hair pull by James Tarkowski on Caleb Yirenkyi. Then in the second half, when Thierno Barry scored to put the Toffees 2-1 up and the ball appeared to come off his hand.

The controversy continued in Saturday's early kick-off between Leeds and Tottenham. First, Leeds wanted a penalty for handball by Mateus Fernandes, though replays did show the ball hit the Spurs player's shoulder.

Then came the potential red card for a challenge by Jayden Bogle on Mathys Tel, which has split opinion. The VAR, Tony Harrington, eventually decided after a four-minute VAR check that the foul did not have enough force.

That Tel was forced off injured, and referee John Brooks did not even show a yellow card on the field, only added to the frustration for Tottenham .

So on to the Emirates, and again the debate was around VAR.

It's a situation few would question. After all, an offside player winning a penalty surely goes against the very logic of the law?

If an offside player is running to the ball and is fouled before they attempt to play the ball or challenge an opponent, then the foul is considered to come before the offside offence.

The law seeks to prevent situations whereby defenders have carte blanche to foul attackers, just because the opponent is offside.

But is a complex area of law and is very much open to interpretation.

In February 2019, the season before VAR came in, an offside Harry Kane was awarded a late penalty in a north London derby after being dragged down by Shkodran Mustafi.

Two years ago, Newcastle were awarded a spot-kick against Bournemouth through a VAR intervention when Adam Smith tugged back an offside Fabian Schar.

Yet last December, after being awarded a penalty against Leeds , Brentford 's Dango Ouattara was ruled to be offside and the spot-kick ruled out through VAR.

So which interpretation is correct? Kane and Schar, or Havertz and Ouattara?

Ouattara was somewhat different, as he appeared to be engaging with Gabriel Gudmundsson as the ball was played.

The Havertz example is more like the one involving Schar, who was running forward when his shirt was tugged back.

But there is an additional consideration, and this is where Oliver's thinking will lie.

Officials are asked to consider the likelihood of the attacker becoming involved in the play from a second phase. Let's say the ball could be first played by a team-mate, which then makes them onside. Then they are not purely benefitting from being offside.

In the case of Schar and Kane, they could have benefitted from that second phase.

Havertz was the only attacker who had any chance of being involved in the play, so the VAR determined offside was the fair outcome.

At least tonight most of the talk will be about another victory for Arsenal - and not VAR.

Goal caps eye-catching Odegaard display - player ratings for Arsenal v Hull

Sometimes we are trying to score the perfect goal - Arteta

Another game, another win but still Arsenal are looking for their attack to spark into life.

At the end of the day results matter but Arsenal , despite being top, are the lowest scorers of the teams in the top four.

They have the best defence in the league and arguably Europe but goals are also seeming hard to come by at the other end.

Arsenal have not scored more than twice in the league since the opening day of the season, when they put three past Coventry .

Arteta's side are missing talisman Bukayo Saka, who is out with a quadricep injury, and has a unique partnership with Ben White and Martin Odegaard on the right.

On the left Christos Tzolis started the season well but, after a hamstring injury while playing for Greece, the 24-year-old has not looked the same threat.

The same can be said for Kai Havertz too.

The 27-year-old picked up a hamstring injury playing for Germany and, even though he scored the winner against Liverpool , his performances have not reached the same level.

Viktor Gyokeres is firmly second choice this season and Arteta is still working out how to get the best out of the maverick Eberechi Eze, while Noni Madueke is working to fill the gap left by Saka.

Arteta was asked about the number of single-goal wins this season and what he can do to improve that.

"To be more efficient," was the answer the Gunners boss gave. "We are one against one against the keeper. That's happened twice today.

"There is a penalty there, there is another situation inside the box where the ball is bouncing. So many shots that have been deflected, blocked. We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic.

"Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And open, I think, score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game."

Even if the Gunners could be more free-flowing going forward, they have started the season in a formidable way - winning nine of their 10 league games.

And if they manage to keep up that rate of winning, the Gunners will likely defend their Premier League crown and win back-to-back titles for the first time in 100 years.

articles.title: Bill Belichick, UNC vs. UConn Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Head coach Bill Belichick's North Carolina Tar Heels went on the road Saturday and scored a 38-21 victory over the UConn Huskies at Pratt & Whitney Stadium in East Hartford, Connecticut.
articles.body:
Head coach Bill Belichick's North Carolina Tar Heels went on the road Saturday and scored a 38-21 victory over the UConn Huskies at Pratt & Whitney Stadium in East Hartford, Connecticut.

UNC was a 7.5-point road favorite, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and it made good on that billing to improve to 5-4 on the season.

Following one of the Tar Heels' best offensive performances of the season, here is a look at the top statistical producers for North Carolina and UConn from Saturday's game:

Both teams got off to a slow start on offense, as the only points in the first quarter came courtesy of Belichick's defense.

Off a deflection, UNC linebacker Timir Hickman-Collins intercepted Huskies quarterback Kalieb Osborne and returned it 62 yards for a touchdown:

That play seemed to heighten the sense of urgency for both offenses, as five of the next six drives ended in touchdowns.

An 18-yard pass from Osborne to wide receiver Ryder Treadway tied the game at 7-7 early in the second quarter:

However, North Carolina answered with its first two offensive touchdowns of the game, as Benjamin Hall scored on a 39-yard run and quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. threw a six-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Shipp:

After Osborne's 24-yard touchdown pass to Cam Abshire to shrink the deficit to seven, the Tar Heels restored their 14-point lead entering halftime, as Edwards hit tight end Jelani Thurman from three yards out with 24 seconds remaining in the opening half:

Early in the third quarter, UConn cut into the North Carolina lead once again when when running back Cyncir Bowers scored a 13-yard rushing touchdown, making it 28-21:

A North Carolina field goal got the lead back into double digits, and after the Tar Heels missed a field goal on their next drive, UConn had a chance to take advantage.

However, Osborne threw his second interception of the day, getting picked off by defensive back Jalon Thompson:

That gave North Carolina great field position, and it took advantage with another short touchdown pass from Edwards to Thurman to put the game away with 3:38 left in the fourth:

UNC ended a two-game losing streak with Saturday's win, and it is now just one victory away from becoming bowl eligible for the first time under Belichick.

The first chance to get that all-important sixth win will come next Saturday when the Tar Heels host the Louisville Cardinals.

As for the Huskies, they have now dropped back-to-back games and fell to 4-5 with the loss on Saturday, and they will try to bounce back next Saturday in a home game against James Madison.

articles.title: Could Arsenal's Ezri Konsa hold off William Saliba from reuniting partnership with Gabriel? Premier League hits and misses

articles.body:
Arsenal did not produce a vintage attacking display against Hull but defensively there were few faults. Their seventh clean sheet in 10 Premier League games, and 10th in 16 overall, owed a lot to their centre-backs. Gabriel and Ezri Konsa excelled again.

William Saliba's impending return will put pressure on Konsa to retain his place but on current form he may keep hold of the shirt. Highlights from his display included a last-ditch block on Mohamed Ali-Cho when was suddenly exposed on the break.

There was no self-congratulation afterwards. Instead he berated the referee for a perceived Hull foul, then got on with business. By the end of the game, he had won all seven of his duels and completed all but two of his 53 passes, a picture of composure.

He continues to make an immense contribution since his arrival at the club. Arsenal had one early scare when Elliot Stroud forced a save from David Raya but it is now 444 minutes without conceding a goal in the Premier League for the Gunners.

Martin Odegaard won it but Konsa did his bit too. Saliba, who will build his fitnesby appearing for Arsenal's U21s on Sunday, has his work to do to win back his place. Nick Wright

Oliver Glasner had suggested after Nottingham Forest's loss to Brentford that the time had come to make changes. And that was true even before kick-off because he delivered the team-talk. "I have played more than 500 games as a player," said Glasner. "I have managed more than 500 games as a manager. I have never heard such an inspiring speech to the team." Yates backed it up on the pitch too. Adam Bate

The question that Manchester City supporters might be asking right now is whether Yates and Xaver Schlager nipping at heels and Jair Cunha pressing up the pitch should have been enough for their side to unravel as they did. Three defeats in a row tells a tale.

"Today we didn't match the intensity, we need to understand the reasons why," said Maresca. "If you make a mistake or you don't win duels, you can concede on transition."

Josko Gvardiol was dispossessed for the first goal, Elliot Anderson was too weak for the second and Marc Guehi made it too easy as well. City look like a side who want to be allowed to play their football but when teams refuse to give them that time then they become unsettled.

Seven wins in a row to start the season suggested that, for all the issues engulfing City right now, it would be a seamless transition under Enzo Maresca on the pitch. But the blueprint for stopping them is now becoming clear. And that should be a major concern. Adam Bate

Are Spurs back? On this evidence, they are not.

Three consecutive wins had raised hopes that Tottenham may have turned a corner amid talk of a European push.

But the limp 1-0 loss at Leeds, which was fully deserved as Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi admitted himself, shows the north London side have plenty of work to do - especially in front of goal.

Spurs created just one big chance at Elland Road and were not good enough, even amidst the controversy of Jayden Bogle's red-card escape.

James Trafford's only meaningful save came from Jan Paul van Hecke's stoppage-time header. The defender is Tottenham's top Premier League scorer this season.

Dominic Solanke failed to have a shot despite coming on in the 43rd minute as Spurs mustered an expected goals of just 0.77 to Leeds' 2.02.

Tottenham have had the second-most shots in the Premier League this season, but have only hit 10 goals.

Spurs' goal-scoring issues will be a major area of work over the international break for De Zerbi if he is to truly get Spurs back fighting for European qualification. Declan OIley

A superb second-half performance from Leeds was deservedly rewarded by a Noah Okafor's winner over Spurs.

His goal was Daniel Farke's making after he brought him and the man who assisted, Harry Wilson, on together as the pair combined just 97 seconds after entering the pitch.

This is a much-needed win for the Whites, who had gone off the boil after starting the season brightly with eight points from their first four league games to go third.

A first win since mid-September will have Leeds fans dreaming again of a potential European push, with their defence central to this.

The clean sheet against Spurs means Arsenal and Brighton remain the only two teams to have conceded fewer goals than Leeds.

And summer-signing Tarik Muharemovic is at the heart of this solidity, having made a match-high 13 clearances in the Spurs win. In fact, his 85 in total is the most of any player in the Premier League this season.

Elland Road also remains a fortress for Leeds, who are now unbeaten in their last nine Premier League home games (W5 D4).

It just feels like the November international break has now come at the wrong time for Leeds and Farke. Declan Olley

Newcastle's display at Fulham may not have been pretty but it was close to the perfect away performance - and may have been but for VAR.

Matthias Jaissle had come under increasing pressure following four defeats in five. He could not argue with the noise surrounding St James' Park after a double-header with Everton saw them drop out of the Carabao Cup and suffer a limp home league defeat within three days last week.

This was the moment he needed to put out a call to his team to show they were still playing for their manager. And they answered.

Despite Fulham's domination, Newcastle had the better of the chances at Craven Cottage and restricted their hosts to an xG of 0.62, the most frugal of any visiting defence this season.

Jaissle talked of "complete commitment and togetherness" in the Magpies' performance - and it was hard to argue.

He might not have had the victory he desired to diffuse the pressure around his position, but the performance still went most of the way. Ron Walker

Coventry may end up in the Premier League relegation zone this weekend, but there's so much positivity from Frank Lampard's side that they will be out of it in no time.

Had the two wrong penalty calls gone their way - and the fine margins about Thierno Barry's second goal for Everton also fallen in their favour - they would have surely picked up three precious points.

And it would have been deserved too. At the back, Stephen Mfuni and Ethan Pinnock look a perfect blend between youth and experience. Caleb Yirenkyi and Jack Rudoni look to have finally caught up with the demands of the Premier League in midfield. Taiwo Awoniyi is a handful up front.

What let them down on Merseyside was the officials and most importantly VAR - perhaps the biggest difference between Championship and Premier League football in this modern era.

With Crystal Palace and Ipswich to come in their next two home games, Lampard's Sky Blues have to shake this disappointment off quickly. The international break will help with that. Sam Blitz

Who had Thierno Barry down as Everton's answer to Erling Haaland? Well, the numbers are starting to look rather similar.

Barry's double against Coventry took him to 10 goals and three assists in all competitions, already surpassing his entire goal tally from last season. Better still, he has now scored in three successive games for Everton for the first time. Suddenly, the Frenchman is discovering a taste for goals that even the most optimistic Evertonian would have struggled to predict.

However, no player in the Premier League has missed more big chances this season than Barry too, with 13. That's an extraordinary number and suggests his finishing has been anything but clinical. Barry was even seen watching the replays of his goals on the big screen at the end of the win over Coventry where he remarked on how efficient he'd been with his finishing. Even he seemed surprised.

Had he been more ruthless this season, his numbers could be even more spectacular. The challenge now is keeping this remarkable consistency in front goal. If he does, then Haaland may have company in the Golden Boot race. Lewis Jones
