articles.title: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Man City: Enzo Maresca's dream start turns into nightmare
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca left the City Ground on Saturday evening with chants of "can we play you every week?" ringing in his ears - the Italian's dream start as Manchester City manager is rapidly turning into a nightmare.
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca left the City Ground on Saturday evening with chants of "can we play you every week?" ringing in his ears - and the Italian's dream start as Manchester City manager is rapidly turning into a nightmare.

Amid a sea of noise from the home faithful on the banks of the River Trent, the delirious Forest supporters witnessed their side produce a thrilling performance as City sunk to a third straight Premier League loss.

Maresca's leaky backline continues to make defensive blunders and once Josko Gvardiol gave the ball away for Jair Cunha to open the scoring in the sixth minute, City were on the back foot.

With Arsenal edging past Hull earlier in the day and keeping another clean sheet, City head into the international break searching for answers after a 3-1 loss and six points behind the champions.

Maresca said: "The first half we didn't match [Forest's] intensity or win duels or second balls. The first thing required in these games is intensity.

"We tried to react at 2-0 but it's too late. We scored one, probably could have scored more but in transition we concede one more. No panic. We need to understand but no panic."

Asked why the intensity was low, Maresca replied: "I need to analyse that."

The situation already looks bleak for City, but what does history show?

Should Brighton fail to beat Brentford on Sunday, Arsenal would be just the fourth side in Premier League history to have a six-point lead after 10 games, while only two teams have been so far behind as City at this stage and gone on to win the title.

One of those was Manchester United in 2002-03. The other? City themselves in 2013-14 under Manuel Pellegrini.

But Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton have the opportunity to leap up to second place and five points behind the Gunners should they beat Brentford .

There is another factor which looms large over City's campaign.

The club have lodged an appeal after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules .

That process is ongoing - and it is not yet known what potential sanctions City could face.

But - even if any possible punishment does not affect this season - their title hopes are looking slimmer by the match.

Delightful Delap and outfought Anderson - Forest v Man City player ratings

Has Anderson lived up to the hype after Man City move?

With his hands tucked inside his trouser pockets and his head bowed, a forlorn-looking Maresca paced the touchline towards the end of the match.

The City boss said during the week he was still getting to know his players, but performances like the one against Forest will provide some clarity as to who he can, and cannot, trust.

After starting the season with seven straight wins, City have hit real trouble with defeats against Aston Villa , Brighton and now a pumped-up Forest.

Their problems at the back are not helping as it was another game where individual errors cost them dearly - and former striker Liam Delap took full advantage of the lapses in concentration with two goals.

Gvardiol was at fault for the first, Iliman Ndiaye and Elliot Anderson got in a muddle for the second, while Matheus Nunes did not put a challenge in for the third.

"Before the game all the talk was about individual errors," former Forest winger Steve Stone told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Apart from the first goal, this hasn't been about that - the line is disjointed.

"The full-backs were very wide. If the ball turns over quickly and you pass it with your first pass you can be right through them. They have been exposed today.

"Oliver Glasner's team have played through them every time."

It was a miserable return to the City Ground for Anderson since his £116m move to City in the summer and the midfield dynamic alongside Enzo Fernandez does not seem to be working.

The Argentine should have scored with a headed chance from close range but spent much of the game complaining in referee Sam Barrott's ear - City team-mates and supporters may be expecting more from their club record signing.

The former Chelsea player scored in the midweek Champions League win at RB Leipzig, but that is his only goal or assist in his past nine games.

Maresca needs to work out how to get the best out of Fernandez during the international break.

Stone added: "I came here tonight thinking City would win, I thought they had chances. This is a real hammer blow to them, there is something not right about the back four at the minute.

"I have never seen a City team give the ball away so much in the middle of the park."

Rayan Cherki's stunning strike gave City hope but they could not turn it around and the numbers following the result make for grim:

City have lost three consecutive Premier League games for the first time since a run of four in November-December 2024

They have become the second team in English top-flight history - after Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05 - to win their first seven games of a season and then lose their next three

This was their first league defeat by two or more goals against a side starting the day in the relegation zone since November 2008 (a 2-0 loss to Bolton Wanderers).

Maresca was forced to chop and change his defence again, withdrawing both Gvardiol and Marc Guehi at half-time because of injuries, according to the manager.

It meant Nunes came in at right-back, with Abdukodir Khusanov moving inside, and Nico O'Reilly playing down the left.

Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy told BBC Sport: "I thought City's performance was poor in terms of mentality.

"To make so make so many mistakes when you go anywhere in the Premier League, but especially to a team who are fighting for the lives, and you know they're going to come after you.

"They were sloppy with the ball, not winning duels. I would even probably go as far as saying there was probably a bit of arrogance at the start of the game from them.

"I think that there are now some big questions to ask the manager about how he gets them back on track. I think with the talent they have got, it is not going to be a big problem.

"But I think defensively, maybe sticking to the same backline for a little while is the way forward."

articles.title: Round 11: Juventus vs. Fiorentina match preview
articles.summary: Juventus are at the final game of their insane four-week stretch of fixtures, and it’s a trip to Florence that could set the tone for the upcoming interntion...
articles.body:
It was a little over a month ago in which we all sat here and thought about just how crazy Juventus' schedule was about to get . Once the longest international break there's ever been was a thing of the past, there would be very little time to breathe, with nine games in 29 days about to consume every bit of Juventus' domestic and European aspirations.

Well, I have an announcement to make, folks: We are 90 minutes away from the end of this hectic nine-game run. One more game and then another international break will arrive, with hopefully some sort of respite for the players who have been logging a whole lot of minutes over the course of the last four weeks.

But, there's still that one final game to go. And it is a game that will come at a venue in which Juve will receive one of their foulest receptions all season.

That's right, it's a trip to Florence that is the one game that separates Juventus and the November international break. Sunday night's matchup at the Franchi will again have Juve trying to do something they haven't done since the opening two weeks of the 2026-27 season — win back-to-back games. It will potentially be accomplished against a Fiorentina side that has struggled out of the gate yet again, with La Viola having the distinction of being the first Serie A club to fire their manager this season and still sit just above the relegation zone through the first 10 games of the new campaign.

Yet, it's hard to forget what happened the last time these two teams played back in the spring. And it's even harder to forget the implications in which that loss at the Allianz had on which European competition Juventus would end up playing in come the new season.

So, maybe in a way it's a little ironic that Juve's first game of the season against Fiorentina comes all of 72 hours after Luciano Spalletti's squad recorded a win in the Europa League. Why? Because that loss is, at least in part, as to why Juve fell out of the Champions League places in the Serie A standings and now playing in the Europa League. There are other factors, obviously, but it's that loss, with all of a couple of games left to go, that ended up putting the nail in the coffin of Juve's UCL hopes.

(Or maybe you want to describe all of that a little bit differently. I will not argue with that.)

For one last Thursday-Sunday combination of fixtures before another international break arrives, Juventus will try and do what they haven't always done after Europa League games this season. It's the very complicated concept of "play well." After their first three Europa League games of the season, Juve's done the following when they return to Serie A that weekend:

OK, so two wins in three games right after the Europa League fixture on Thursdays is not horrible, but the way they've played in those three games that is probably just as much of a lasting impression than the result itself. They played well against Atalanta, they were terrible against Lazio and then they were a little bit of both against Lecce. It's something that sums up the last few years of Juve on the whole, with there certainly being more bad than good on the whole.

So now against a Fiorentina side that has won all of two games in Serie A so far this season — remember, it's November! — Juve will be adding their latest chapter to the "How will they do after a Europa League fixture?" narrative that we've already see take shape. And just like when Juventus had less than 72 hours to try and prepare for their weekend fixture after beating Celta Vigo last month, Spalletti's squad will have a quick turnaround and then play an away fixture at one of the most hostile environments they'll face all season.

Fiorentina are not good again this season. But we said that last season, too. And when we said that last season, Fiorentina went on to take points off Juventus both times. So, in that sense, it hasn't really mattered what kind of form Fiorentina are in because they've been able to prevent Juve from beating them for the past two seasons.

With some of the other fixtures going on Sunday, there's a chance for Juventus to get closer to the pack that is currently in front of them in the European places. But the thing that Juve has to do is take care of their business as well before some of their roster goes off on international duty for the better part of the next two weeks.

That's not something they've done against Fiorentina in recent years — which, considering the current state of the club that calls the Franchi home, is not exactly a glowing endorsement of things happening at Continassa.

So let's hope Juve can buck the trend of their matchup against Fiorentina from the last couple of years. That would be a nice way to go into the break — and certainly a change for the better compared to how things went the last time they faced that team from Florence that wears purple.

Spalletti didn't hold a pre-match press conference this weekend, so we don't know the condition of a handful of players who may or may not be called up to face Fiorentina.

The one player who looks set to miss out on the trip to Florence is Andrea Cambiaso, who is reportedly dealing with a muscle strain coming out of the win over AZ Alkmaar on Thursday.

That means Cambiaso is added to the injury list that also includes Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khephren Thuram, Francisco Conceição, Nico González and Kamil Grabara.

There is hope that both Weston McKennie — who was held out of Thursday's trip to the Netherlands out of precaution — and Zeki Çelik will both be called up to face Florence. Çelik has been out since Juve's draw with Stade Rennes on Oct. 22.

Juventus have not won any of their last four games against Fiorentina, with a loss and a draw in both of the last two seasons when facing La Viola.

This will be the 175th time that Juventus and Fiorentina have played each other in Serie A.

We know that the starting lineup that Spalletti rolls out in Florence this weekend will look a lot like the one he used a few days earlier in the Europa League simply because of who is actually available to play. Not that it is anything new — rotating the squad has been fairly limited because of how many injuries there have been.

Because of that, the choices here are probably the same as they were ahead of Thursday in Alkmaar.

So why not go with the young man who is easily one of the players a whole lot of us have enjoyed watch more and more as his time in bianconero has gone on these last few weeks? Yes, we are going to talk about Kerim.

As much as Randal Kolo Muani was the standout performer against Napoli last weekend, it's Kerim Alajbegović that has rightly or wrongly had a lot put on his young shoulders during this hectic run of games simply because he's one of Juventus' true creative attacking players who is actually healthy right now.

Alajbegović has not taken Serie A by storm during his first handful of starts as a Juve player, but his stunning goal against Napoli was just proof of what he can do when things are going right. You combine that with some of the nifty footwork and moves he's put on opposing defenders — everybody go ask Giovanni Di Lorenzo how he's doing after that Juve win over Napoli — and those flashes have been present as well.

But, with all of that being said, he's 19 years old and getting used to play in a new league that is much tougher on attacking players — especially young ones — than the one that he played in last season.

So why Alajbegović as the pick here? Because he will be facing a Fiorentina defense that is … not good. Yep, not good at all. La Viola haven't posted a shutout since the middle of September — and that was in the Coppa Italia against a team that is currently playing in Serie B. (And just so happened to hire Damien Comolli is their new CEO, so that can tell you how things might be going at Pisa these days since they got relegated in the spring.)

This feels like the kind of game that could see Alajbegović be one of the driving forces of a Juventus win. Those two things will likely go together just as they did last weekend at the Allianz. And if he does that and Juve get their first win over Fiorentina since the final weeks of Max Allegri's second stint in charge, then it will be a pretty good way to go into the international break.

Where: Stadio Artemio Franchi, Florence, Italy.

Official kickoff time: 8:45 p.m. local time in Italy and across Europe, 7:45 p.m. in the United Kingdom, 2:45 p.m. Eastern time, 1:45 p.m. Central time, 11:45 a.m. Pacific time.
